trickyParts: The proof above ran at ddb96cfd5b58. The reviewed head is 2843635fe941, and the only code change between them is packages/claude-envoy/dist/envoy-channel.js, a generated bundle whose single changed line is `daemonApiVersion: 32` → `33` and which the pod builder never reads. The pod-builder suite, the podsafety suite and the shim suite are green at 2843635fe941 in the `Tests` run 39403205418 (jobs lint, typecheck, test), and the claude-envoy job of `Legion Envoy and Contracts` run 39403205468 is green there, where it failed at ddb96cfd5b58 on the stale bundle alone.

A role container's plain environment never appears in the pod template, so the eight golden Sandbox manifests are byte-identical after this change and `-update` leaves them untouched: launcherContainers sets only the kubelet-resolved variables (POD_UID, the operator's secret refs), and every NAME=value pair travels in the launcher's start command (launchEnvironment). The tests that carry the proof are TestEachRoleIsToldAScratchDirectoryOfItsOwnOnTheIssueVolume, which reads workerOf's container plus the start command's environment, and TestTheRuntimeTellsTheShimEveryScratchDirectoryItMakes.

TMPDIR goes from /tmp (4 bytes) to /legion/scratch/<role>/tmp (26-31 bytes) and Linux's sun_path holds 107, so three cmd/legion tests that listen on filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "s") failed with `bind: invalid argument` under the new value. Fixed in this pull request (socketDir); two further copies of the same helper elsewhere in the module carry the same latent limit and are the PR's one Fast-follow line.

podsafety.EnsureScratch deliberately does not make XDG_STATE_HOME: EnsureStateHome makes Oh My Pi's profile directory under it, and its refusal carries its own reason. The one list the two sides share is podsafety.ScratchVariables, locked to the runtime's rendering by a sandbox test, because a name added to roleEnvironment and not to that list would leave a role told a temporary directory nothing created.

The change validated itself under the failure it fixes: this implementer's pod was replaced twice (08:16Z and 08:18:53Z on 2026-10-20) during `go build ./...` with the Go caches on the container's filesystem, and the identical cold build then completed in 115 s with no replacement once those caches pointed at /legion/scratch. The planner lost its container the same way while measuring bun's 1.4 GB cache.

Adding four names to runtimeOwned refuses, at boot, any deployment whose runtime.kubernetes.pod.env sets one of them. This is settled, not open: the architect read the deployment on 2026-10-20 at 08:10Z and every project there sets exactly one pod environment variable, DISPATCH_PUBLIC_URL, with ANTHROPIC_API_KEY and OPENAI_API_KEY as its provider keys, so none of TMPDIR, GOCACHE, GOMODCACHE or BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR collides and pinning the new image refuses no boot. No human has anything to confirm here; the first commit of this handoff carried it as an open question in error, and the plan's own stale line was removed in plan.md version 2.
deviations: The plan's task 5 says the eight golden Sandbox manifests are regenerated. They are not, and must not be, for the reason in trickyParts; `go test ./internal/runtime/sandbox/ -update` was run and left them byte-identical.

The plan's task 5 does not name packages/claude-envoy/package.json, which also declares legion.daemonApiVersion and is held to the fixture by packages/claude-envoy/tests/daemon-api-version.test.ts. It is moved to 33 with the other two, and both CHANGELOGs carry the entry.

Two further documentation surfaces the plan does not name were found by the grep its task 6 prescribes and corrected: docs/site/src/content/docs/legion/running-legion.md (the published page repeating the ephemeral-storage sentence) and docs/kubernetes.md's controller-pod paragraph (the controller is a role container too). The two docs/solutions/legion/ LEGION-632 learnings keep their account of what happened and say that the state home and the caches have moved since.

The plan's acceptance for the bun criterion names `bun add --exact --backend=copyfile is-odd@3.0.1` with `stat -c %h` as the live half. That command was not run here, and the architect has corrected the reasoning: what killed the planner was a cold install of this whole repository at the default cache location, not this check, which installs one tiny package with BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR on the issue volume and writes a few kilobytes. It is cheap and it is the only live evidence for the copying acceptance line, so the architect has asked the tester to run it in its own phase. The rendered-script assertion and the planner's own measurement (one link per file with the flag, one shared inode without) are this phase's proof.
One fix outside the plan's six tasks: worker_shim_test.go's socketDir. It is a consequence of the change (sun_path against the new TMPDIR), not unrelated cleanup, and it is in its own commit.
discoveredComplexity: Nothing prunes /legion/scratch: a role's temporary files and caches now outlive the pod that wrote them and live until the issue closes. Six roles that all build come to roughly 14 GB against a 20 GiB issue volume, which the plan records and the issue's asks accept; issue_volume is the operator's lever.

A full issue volume now also stops a pod from starting, because the shim refuses when it cannot make a directory, where today a full volume leaves the roles running. Nothing in the daemon watches a volume's free space.
